task.title: A grade and admission to an olympiad
task.description: The platform sets score (0–100) and age. Declare let grade and with an if / else if / else chain assign a numeric grade: 90 and above - 5, from 75 - 4, from 60 - 3, below - 2. Declare const canEnter - admission to an olympiad: age from 14 and score from 60. Declare const status with a ternary operator: "Admitted" or "Not admitted". Print with a template string: Grade: 4. Admitted. Use strict comparisons only.

tests.name: 87 points → grade 4
tests.fail: Check the chain: 87 >= 75 but less than 90.

tests.name: 95 points → 5
tests.fail: Check the strictest condition first: score >= 90.

tests.name: 74 points → 3
tests.fail: 74 is less than 75 but not less than 60 - that is 3.

tests.name: 59 points → 2
tests.fail: Below 60 - the else branch, grade 2 (a number, no quotes).

tests.name: Age 13 and 95 points - not admitted
tests.fail: BOTH conditions are needed: the && operator, not ||.

tests.name: Admission boundaries: age 14 and 60 points - admitted
else if is used
tests.fail: Write the grade choice as an if / else if / else chain.

tests.name: status is chosen with a ternary operator
The program runs without errors
tests.fail: There is an error in the code - read its text in the console.

hints: Declare let grade; before if, and only assign in the branches: grade = 5;
Order: first score >= 90, then >= 75, then >= 60, else at the end.
The grade is a number: grade = 5; without quotes.

questions.question: What does this code print: const t = 30; if (t > 25) { console.log("Hot"); } else { console.log("Warm"); }
questions.explanation: 30 > 25 is true, the first branch runs and else is skipped.

questions.question: score = 95. What does this print: if (score >= 60) { console.log("Pass"); } else if (score >= 90) { console.log("Excellent"); }
questions.explanation: The first matching branch runs. Strict conditions go first.

questions.question: Which operator means "AND"? Type it.
questions.explanation: a && b is true only if both are true.

questions.question: Which values are falsy?
questions.explanation: Non-empty strings, even "0" and "false", are truthy.

questions.question: How do you correctly write "hour from 6 to 11 inclusive"?
questions.explanation: Two comparisons joined with &&. 6 <= hour <= 11 is always true.

questions.question: What does this print: const age = 20; console.log(age >= 18 ? "Adult" : "Child");
questions.explanation: The condition is true - the value before the colon is taken.

questions.question: Match the expression with the result.
What happens in if (role = "admin") { ... }?
options: Assignment: role becomes "admin", the block runs

questions.question: What is true about switch?
options: default runs if no case matched
It is handy for ranges like score >= 90

questions.question: In a switch, break is missing after case "mon". What happens when day = "mon"?
options: Execution continues into the next case

questions.question: How many branches run in an if / else if / else chain? Type a number.
questions.explanation: Exactly one - the first matching one or else.
